title: add VPC control plane provisioning: multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: provide a repeatable, multi-AZ Terraform module and installer hooks to provision the VPC-based private control plane network for private deployments. This PR adds a control-plane VPC module (subnets across 3 AZs), private interface endpoints for SSM/EC2/ECR/S3, security group templates with least-privilege defaults for control-plane components, cross-account VPC peering helpers, Route53 private hosted zone and resolver rules for cross-account DNS forwarding, and installer upgrade hooks to migrate existing single-AZ networks to the new multi-AZ layout. The description below summarizes files, commits, testing, and reviewer feedback. Checklist: [x] Terraform module for vpc/control-plane [x] Multi-AZ subnet allocation and AZ-aware route tables [x] Interface endpoints: com.amazonaws.*.ssm, ec2, ecr.dkr, s3 [x] Security group templates and example policies [x] Cross-account peering option and IAM role bootstrapping docs [x] Route53 private hosted zone + outbound resolver rules for DNS peering [x] Installer post-deploy hooks and rollback instructions [x] Unit tests (terraform validate) and CI integration tests. Acceptance criteria: terraform plan applies cleanly in test account, cross-account peering can be created with the helper iam role, Installer can perform zero-downtime rollout when migrating existing control-plane VPCs. Breaking changes: none by default; migration path is opt-in. See release_notes for user-facing items and upgrade_notes for operational steps.
commits: feat(terraform): add control-plane vpc module with multi-az subnets and route tables
feat(terraform): add interface endpoint resources and route53 resolver rules
chore(installer): wire module into private-installer provisioning workflow
feat(security): add security group templates and least-privilege examples
docs: add README and upgrade guide for migrating single-AZ to multi-AZ
review_comments: Miguel Torres (review): Please ensure subnets are evenly distributed across AZs and include explicit cidr_block_count/az mapping. Also prefer using aws_eip for nat gateway tracking in examples.
Asha (author): Updated subnet allocation to use az_count and explicit az mapping; added note about reserved CIDR for future node pools.
Lina Zhang (security): SGs look permissive to start. Can we restrict control-plane SG to only allow API traffic from load balancer subnets and mTLS ports between control-plane nodes?
Asha (author): Tightened SG rules, added example that shows ALB-only ingress and mutual TLS port 9443 restricted to control-plane SG. Added tests for SG policy generation.
Owen McCarthy (network): Cross-account peering helper is useful but needs clear IAM boundary docs. Add tests or scripts for peering acceptance in CI.
Asha (author): Added acceptance script and documented trust policy. Marked peering as opt-in with explicit flag to avoid surprise costs.
Lina Zhang (security): Please add a short runbook for rollback if resolver rules fail during migration.
Asha (author): Added rollback instructions to installer hooks and the docs/upgrade guide.

CI bot: terraform validate passed on changeset; terraform plan shows no destructive changes for default flags; integration tests initially failed on resolver rule propagation, fixed by adding route53 wait-for-propagation step.
Reviewer approval: Lina Zhang approved on 2024-11-14. Miguel Torres approved on 2024-11-14.
Merge: Squash-merged by Lina Zhang on 2024-11-15.
release_notes: Added Terraform module to provision a multi-AZ VPC for private control plane deployments
Added support for private interface endpoints (SSM, EC2, ECR, S3) and Route53 resolver rules for cross-account DNS
Introduced security group templates with least-privilege defaults for control-plane components
Installer includes optional post-deploy migration hooks to migrate single-AZ control planes to the new multi-AZ layout
test_plan: Run terraform validate and plan in a sandbox account
Provision control-plane VPC in test account with default flags
Create optional cross-account peering using helper IAM role in a separate test account
Run installer post-deploy migration hook against an existing single-AZ control plane (dry-run first)
Verify Route53 resolver rules and DNS propagation between accounts
upgrade_notes: Migration is opt-in: set enable_multi_az = true in installer config to run post-deploy hooks
Installer will create new subnets and backbone resources; control-plane pods are drained and moved with zero-downtime rollout
If Route53 resolver rules fail to propagate, follow rollback steps in docs/upgrade/migrate-control-plane-multi-az.md
risk: Medium: networking and cross-account DNS changes carry blast radius. Defaults are conservative and peering must be explicitly enabled. We added wait-for-propagation and rollback steps to mitigate.
